subject: Token fanout latency wave — FlowMart tenant coordination & customer note
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: engineering-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T08:12:00Z
Subject: [Incident] p95 token fanout spike observed for FlowMart tenant

Team —

Quick summary: starting ~2027-05-01T07:50:00Z we saw a sustained p95 jump from ~120ms -> ~780ms for FlowMart (tenant id fm-prod-42) on gen-api. Errors are minimal but latency is causing user-facing degradation (chat input lag, some timeouts). Scope seems limited to requests with long contexts (>2k tokens) and include a new prompt pattern that causes increased KV cache churn.

What we know:
- A rollout of model variant gpt-open-3-v2.3-quant landed to canary -> prod yesterday (2027-04-30) and we changed kernel scheduling parameters in the same push.
- Metrics show increased per-token processing time and elevated queue times on shard gpu-7a.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) for FlowMart dropped ~35% during the window; other tenants on same pool degraded but less severely.

Immediate data attached: p95-spike-kernel-logs.txt (sampled spans, kernel traces).

Immediate ask:
1) Can product/eng weigh a quick pin/rollback of FlowMart to pre-v2.3 variant (v2.2) while we investigate?
2) SRE: can we enable per-tenant static KV cache for FlowMart as a temporary mitigation?
3) CS/Account: need a short customer note draft we can send by EOD acknowledging impact + ETA for mitigation.

I can keep running diagnostics and will provide a live link to traces in SUP-1129.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[attachment: p95-spike-kernel-logs.txt (text/plain)]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@flowmart.com>
Cc: cs-ops@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: [Incident] p95 token fanout spike observed for FlowMart tenant

Thanks Dylan —

Alex: apologies for the interruption this morning. Looping in product and eng so we can coordinate an immediate mitigation and customer comms. For transparency: we believe the rollout of v2.3-quant + kernel scheduling changes increased per-token latency in cases with repeated long-context prompts (token fanout effect), which is hitting FlowMart harder because of several multi-turn flows.

Immediate proposal (operational):
- Pin FlowMart to model variant v2.2 for 60m while we confirm root cause (requires a quick rollout change on Dedicated routing).
- Enable per-tenant static KV caching and length cutoff at 3k tokens for FlowMart to reduce cache churn (SRE action).
- Apply soft rate-limit at 12 rps for some high-cost routes for the next 2 hours to avoid throughput collapse.

Product / Roadmap ask:
- We should prioritize a toggle in the console to pin model variant per-tenant (fast rollback for prod customers) — is this feasible as a hotfix?

Attached is a customer note draft (flowmart-cust-note-draft.txt) — please review/edit.

Dylan — can you confirm the rollback timeline and whether the static KV cache toggle is low-risk? Karthik/Marissa, flag any product constraints.

Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[attachment: flowmart-cust-note-draft.txt (text/plain)]

Thanks — good catch Dylan. Quick answers:

- We can push a per-tenant pin to v2.2; engineering estimates ~20 minutes to stage and validate before switching traffic. We'll need SRE to confirm the routing change and to prepare rollback playbook windows.
- Console toggle: this is not currently exposed to ops as a one-click action; we have a half-day patch that exposes variant pinning for org-level admins. I can coordinate a hotfix and cut a safe launch with a feature-flag; estimate 24-36 hours to ship, but we can do a targeted emergency deployment to unblock pinning for FlowMart only if legal/CS sign-off.
- KV static caching as mitigation: SRE + infra should be able to toggle this per-tenant; note it will increase memory footprint.

Customer communication suggestion: be explicit about the mitigation timeline, what we're doing (pin + cache toggle + rate limiting), and offer a small credit (e.g., 1 week of service credit or 10% invoice credit) if the impact affects SLA. I'll defer to CS for final wording.

I'm attaching the rollback playbook we use for model variant switches.

—Marissa

Thanks for your patience. Quick summary of what we're doing now and what to expect in the next hour: 

1) Immediate mitigations (in progress)
- Pinning your tenant to model variant v2.2 (expected completion ~20 minutes)
- Enabling per-tenant static KV caching and applying a soft route-level rate cap to stabilize throughput

2) Investigation: our SREs are validating kernel traces to confirm whether the v2.3 scheduling changes increased per-token compute in long-context paths. We will share a technical summary in SUP-1129 once validated.

3) Customer impact & remediation: You may see occasional latency during the change window as we shift traffic; we plan to monitor closely and rollback if instability increases. If you'd like, we can schedule a short call after the mitigation to review traces and next steps.

4) Compensation: as a gesture for the interruption, we propose a one-week service credit or 10% invoice credit — open to whichever is preferred by your finance team.

Please let me know if you want an immediate call. We'll keep you updated every 30 minutes while the change is active.

Best,
